Calibrating Atlantis with MPI Parallelism

atlantiscalibration

2026-11-18

calibrate_MPI.Rmd

Overview

This vignette describes how to calibrate an Atlantis ecosystem model with the calibrar package. The example uses the South East Australia Atlantis model (SETAS) and is designed to run on a multi-core server or HPC cluster.

The calibration estimates multiplicative factors for selected biological and fishing parameters of the model. For each parameter and group, calibrar proposes a value p in log scale; the model is run with the original value of the parameter multiplied by exp(p), so p = 0 is the original model. Each model run is compared with targets (biomass, weight at age, abundance at age and catch), and the AHR-ES evolutionary algorithm searches for the factors that best fit all the targets.

The workflow has six steps:

  1. Prepare the model configuration and the input files.
  2. Choose the parameters to calibrate for each functional group.
  3. Create the calibration targets, settings and parameters.
  4. Read the calibration inputs and build the objective function.
  5. Run the calibration in parallel.
  6. Inspect the results.

1. Model configuration and input files

The package uses the following folder structure (all paths are relative to the project root, found with here::here()):

inputs/                       # files created for the calibration
  data/                       # target time series, one CSV per target
  parameter_table.csv         # parameters to calibrate for each group (step 2)
  reproduction-option.csv     # recruitment option of each group (step 2)
  model_configuration/        # all the files needed to run the model
    outputFolder/             # outputs of a previous run of the model
outputs/                      # plots
  keep_track_calibration/     # parameter files used in each run of each iteration

inputs/model_configuration contains the Atlantis model files: functional groups, biology, harvest and run parameter files, initial conditions, forcing, the shell script that runs the model (the only file with extension .sh), and the observed time series used as targets.

Requirements for the model configuration

  • Functional groups file. Add a column IsCalibrated, set to 1 for the groups that are calibrated and 0 for those that are not. Only groups with IsTurnedOn == 1 and IsCalibrated == 1 are calibrated.

  • Shell script. The shell script that runs Atlantis is found by its extension: there must be exactly one .sh file in the model directory. The biology and harvest parameter files are the ones given to its options -b and -h. At every run, run_model() writes the edited parameters to these same files, so the shell script does not need to be changed. The first time it runs in a directory, it keeps a copy of each original file as <file>.original, and the factors are always applied to the values in this copy. read_sh_file() shows the files used by the shell script:

    read_sh_file(here::here("inputs", "model_configuration"))

  • Output time steps. The model outputs are compared with the last dt.timeseries output time steps of each run, so the run length (tstop) and output frequency (toutinc) in the run parameter file must be set so that the last dt.timeseries outputs correspond to the period of the targets. A run is considered crashed if it stops before tstop; all its outputs are then set to zero.

2. Choose the parameters to calibrate

The parameters to calibrate, and the groups each one applies to, are set in inputs/parameter_table.csv. It has one row per functional group (column Code) and one column per parameter, set to 1 if the parameter is calibrated for that group and 0 if not. The optional columns GroupType, IsTurnedOn and IsCalibrated are also used if present.

Column Parameter Edited in
mum Maximum growth rate biology .prm
BHalpha, BHbeta Beverton-Holt recruitment biology .prm
KDENR Recruits per adult biology .prm
mfc Fishing mortality (mFC) harvest .prm
mQ, mL Quadratic and linear mortality biology .prm
C Clearance rate biology .prm
E Assimilation efficiency biology .prm
pprey Food availability biology .prm

It is best to calibrate one parameter per sensitive process. Rules for use:

  • BHalpha, BHbeta and KDENR are only calibrated for vertebrates (GroupType FISH, SHARK, BIRD or MAMMAL).
  • KDENR is only calibrated for groups with recruitment option flagrecruit = 12, and BHalpha and BHbeta for groups with flagrecruit = 3 (Beverton-Holt)

The recruitment option of each group is read from the biology parameter file with repro_option(), which writes inputs/reproduction-option.csv:

atlantiscalibration::repro_option(fg.file, biology.prm)

atlantiscalibration::read_parameter_table(parameter.file)

3. Create the calibration targets, settings and parameters

make_calsettings() creates all the files needed for the calibration:

  • Targets, one CSV per target in inputs/data:

    var.type Target Source Likelihood
    "biomass" <Code>_biomass Initial biomass from a time series file fun.type = lnorm2
    "weight" <Name><age>_w Initial weight at age, from the initial conditions fun.type = lnorm2
    "abundance" <Name>_Nums Initial abundance at age, from the initial conditions fun.type = multinom
    "catch" <Name>_catch Median observed catch fun.type = lnorm2
    "prey" <Code>_prey Proportions from a prey composition file fun.type = lnorm2

    ** Note that prey target requires flagdietcheck 1 in the run.prm

    Each target is constant over dt.timeseries time steps. Biomass targets are created from a biomass time series file (see `create_target_files_biomass().

  • inputs/calibration_settings_*.csv: one CSV file per target type (e.g., calibration_settings_biomass.csv, calibration_settings_abundance.csv), with one row per target in that type. Each row contains the likelihood (type), weight, data file and column (varid). Use w.vector to give different weights to some groups.

  • inputs/calibration-parameters-complete.csv: one row per factor to estimate, named after the parameter and group (e.g. mum_FPS_factor, ZS_mQ_factor), with its initial value (paropt = 0), bounds (parmin = -1, parmax = 1, i.e. factors between exp(-1) = 0.37 and exp(1) = 2.7) and phase (parphase). The bounds and phases can be edited in this file before step 4.


atlantiscalibration::make_calsettings(fg.file = fg.file,
                 var.type       = var.type,
                 fun.type       = fun.type,
                 dt.timeseries  = dt.timeseries,
                 w.vector       = w.vector,
                 biology.prm    = biology.prm,
                 init.file      = init.file,
                 catch.file     = catch.file,
                 run.prm,
                 parameter.file = parameter.file)

fun.type can be any likelihood available in calibrar (see ?calibrar::calibration_setup) or a user-defined function. The package includes likelihood_function(), which penalises simulated values outside a minimum-maximum envelope given by two columns of observed data; to use it, set type to likelihood_function for those targets in any of the calibration_settings_*.csv files.

4. Read the calibration inputs and build the objective function

read_calibration() reads the settings and targets with calibrar, reads the parameters, builds the objective function and sets up the optimiser. The objective function runs the model with run_model(), which, at every parameter proposal:

  1. multiplies the original value of each calibrated parameter by its factor and writes it to the biology (-b) and harvest (-h) parameter files of the shell script,
  2. runs Atlantis with the shell script,
  3. reads the outputs and returns one element per target: biomass by group, weight at age, catch summed over fleets, and abundance at age. If the run crashed, all outputs are zero.

The parameter files used in every model run are saved in outputs/keep_track_calibration (argument track.path), with one folder per iteration (generation) and the run number in the file name:

outputs/keep_track_calibration/
  iteration_001/
    run_001_calibration-parameters.csv        # factors of run 1
    run_001_VMPA_setas_biol_fishing_Trunk.prm # biology parameters of run 1
    run_001_VMPA_setas_harvest_F_Trunk.prm    # harvest parameters, if mfc is calibrated
    run_002_...
  iteration_002/
  ...
  final_001/                                  # best solution at the end of phase 1
    run_000_...

The run number is the calibrar run directory (<run>/i1, <run>/i2, …). The best solution is evaluated again in <run>/i0 at the end of each phase, and saved in final_<phase>. The iteration is counted in each run directory, so it continues correctly when a calibration is restarted.

calibrar copies the master directory to a new directory under run for each model run, so master must contain all the files needed to run the model, and the arguments of run_model() are file names relative to it.

calibration <- atlantiscalibration::read_calibration(
  calibration.settings,  
  calibration.parameters, 
  n.Cores,
  maxgen,
  master,
  run,
  restart.file,
  track.path,
  REPORT,
  parallel,
  no.trace,
  prefix,
  fg.file,
  biom.indx,
  run.prm,
  dt.timeseries
)

The control settings passed to calibrar are:

Setting Value Purpose
maxit / maxgen maxgen Maximum number of generations
popsize n.Cores Model runs per generation
nCores n.Cores Parallel workers; equal to popsize for full parallelism
REPORT 1 Save a restart every generation
trace 3 Report global and per-target fitness

5. Run the calibration

run_calibration() starts a cluster with n.Cores workers, loads the packages and objects each worker needs, and runs the AHR-ES (Adaptive Hierarchical Recombination Evolution Strategy) optimiser, which is well suited to the noisy, expensive fitness evaluations of ecosystem models. Parameters are estimated in the phases given by parphase.

Note: For parallel calibration to work, the atlantiscalibration package must be installed in the system library library(atlantiscalibratio)

If the calibration is interrupted, running it again with the same restart.file continues from the last saved generation.

6. Inspect the results

The results are saved by calibrar in <restart.file>.results. compare_outputs() compares the initial and optimised factors, and plots the fitness of each target for the best solution of each generation:

comparison <- atlantiscalibration::compare_outputs(forcing = calibration$forcing)

comparison$param_comparison  # factor_new: factor applied to the original parameter value
comparison$plot_changes

The trace of the optimisation has the global fitness (results$trace$value), the fitness of each target (results$trace$fitness) and the parameters (results$trace$par) of the best solution of each generation:

results <- readRDS(here::here("inputs","restart_file.results"))

matplot(results$trace$par, type = "l", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Generation", ylab = "Parameter (log factor)")

The calibrated parameter values are the original values multiplied by exp(results$par). To create the calibrated parameter files, run run_model() once with results$par in a copy of the model configuration.

atlantiscalibration::plot_calibration_targets(
    run_dir = here::here("RUN"),
    data_dir = here::here("inputs", "data"),
    settings_dir = here::here("inputs"),
    output_dir = here::here("outputs"),
    parameter_file = here::here("inputs", "parameter_table.csv"),
    output_prefix = "outputSETAS"
    )
